answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a bonded identity graph. Each agent locks real stake before it can vouch for peers, and that bond is slashed once a duplicate self is proven. A bridge is trusted only when both ends carry their own on-ledger collateral, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand real deposits, not a thousand free keys. Verification acts like a prism, splitting each claim into independent checkable links; and no willow of plausible aliases can hide that they share one unfunded root. The attacker pays linearly per fake voice, making mass impersonation unprofitable.
